R. Q. 1 شَرْشَرَهُ , (A 'Obeyd, K,) inf. n. شَرْشَرَةٌ, (S,) He split it, or clave it: (A 'Obeyd, S:) and cut it much, or in many pieces. (A 'Obeyd, S, K.) ―
-b2- He bit it, and then shook it; namely, a thing. (O, K, TA. [In the CK, نَقَضَهُ is erroneously put for نَفَضَهُ.]) ―
-b3- شَرْشَرَتْهُ الحَيَّةُ The serpent bit him. (L, K. *) ―
-b4- شرشرت المَاشِيَةُ النَّبَاتَ The cattle ate the herbage. (K.) ―
-b5- شرشر السِّكِّينَ He sharpened, (K,) or rubbed, (O,) the knife upon a stone, (O, K, TA,) so that its edge became rough. (O, TA.) ―
-b6- See also 1, latter part. ＝
-A2- شَرْشَرَ, inf. n. as above, It (a bird) expanded and flapped its wings, without alighting; like رَفْرَفَ. (TA in art. فرش.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
